title: statement.scope is ignored: a bounded law true within its horizon is REFUTED by a longer witness, and the record's scope comes from its status
reproduction: In the clone, laws/T9/L3_small_bounded.json is a holon-ir/0.3 law over the toy queue: forall p:Trace. small(run(p,s0)) == true, with scope {kind: bounded, H: 2}. It is true for traces of at most 2 actions. `HOLON_BUILD_DIR=../b_scope python3 -m holon run --milestone T9 --no-registry --out ../t9_results --gen-dir ../t9_gen` printed `L3_small_bounded REFUTED checked finding`. The record has scope 'unbounded' and witness {'p': [push 1, push 1, push 1]} (3 actions > H). `grep -rn '"scope"' holon` shows statement.scope is read only when copying it into generated IR (mlaws.py:421, implication.py:61). mlaws.emit, explore.mjs and ir.render_statement never read it. mpipeline.py:505-508 sets rec['scope'] = 'bounded' iff the status is UNKNOWN, so scope is derived from status, the opposite of the plan's 'scope separate from status'. at_state{ref} is likewise ignored.
plan_or_paper_ref: BUILD_PLAN I7 goal 'a scope separate from status', deliverable statement.scope in {unbounded, bounded{H}, at_state{ref}}; whitepaper 8.6 (scope orthogonal to status)
suggested_fix: Emit bounded{H} as a premise len(p) <= H, or a bounded trace type, and bound the explorer by H. at_state needs the referenced state. Until then, reject (Unsupported) any law whose scope is not unbounded. Record statement.scope separately from status in the v2 record. Add a test_ir03 fixture: a bounded-true law must never be REFUTED by a witness longer than H.
resolution: bounded{H} is now checked by the kernel: the emitter (mlaws.Emitter.scope_props) adds len(p) <= H for every universal Trace binder (and a claim conjunct for an existential one). The explorer (explore.mjs) never proposes a longer witness. at_state{ref} is Unsupported. Bounded scope over Reach, or with no Trace binder, is Unsupported. For 0.3 laws, scope, statement_scope and scope_v2 now come from statement.scope and never from status (mpipeline.scope_fields; the v2 schema rules are split, and 0.1/0.2 records keep their pinned meaning). G11V inhabitants keep the scope too (inhabit.inhabitant_ir). New fixtures: L3_small_bounded, L3_small_bounded_false, L3_at_state, L3_bounded_vacuous. Other tests in the same module cover the refuted-within-horizon case, at_state, scope recorded apart from status, and the inhabitant.

title: 0.3 refs miss what a statement depends on and over-cover what it does not: cost/elapsed ignore facts.disch, observers ignore the defs and library builtins they call
reproduction: holon/gen/refs.py:27,65,87-88: _TRACE_FNS (runs_ok, last_ok, no_code, perm, cost, elapsed) map to step_src = {state, initial, params, types, defs, actions}. machine.py:740-751 builds cost and elapsed from facts['disch'], which step_src omits. Reproduction on the M1 facts: a 0.3 law claiming cost(p) == 0. With disch.cost.sendMessage changed from 1 to 101, the hash is unchanged (sha256:3dfc1fa0... both times). Changing disch.delay also leaves the hash unchanged (True). refs.py:71: an obsv ref hashes only facts['observers'][NAME]. A law over lci_of(s) keeps the same hash after def lci drops its '- 1' ('hash equal? True'). refs() takes no library argument, so spec/M1/lib/*.lib.json builtins (nth_ch in kappa, win_last, hdr_of) are in no 0.3 hash. Over-coverage: editing only setPause's 'src' span changes the hash of L_disch_stale taken as 0.3 (True), because 'step' covers every action's source text. Under I13/I15 span keys, any re-extraction that shifts line numbers would therefore restale every site law. The plan's {template_id, template_version} for synthesized helpers, and diagram-element refs from I11, are not implemented. tests_m2/test_ir03 only tests ir.statement_hash with hand-given refs; nothing tests refs().
plan_or_paper_ref: BUILD_PLAN I7 'refs maps each referenced definition to the content hash of the construct that defines it: a facts or lib def ... generator-synthesized helpers map to {template_id, template_version}; no whole-bundle hashes'; whitepaper 8.9 references by hash, 9.4
suggested_fix: Compute refs as the transitive closure over the facts def graph and the library builtins (hash each lib builtin entry). Map cost and elapsed to facts.disch. Give synthesized helpers, including I15's at_site and site_hit, {template_id, template_version}. Exclude doc and src text from the step ref, or key it per action reached. Add refs unit tests: edit a def under an observer, a disch entry and a lib builtin (hash must change), and an unrelated action's src (hash must not). Do this before I15 freezes the first 0.3 hashes into REGISTRY.
resolution: holon/gen/refs.py now computes the transitive closure over the facts def graph and the target library. lib:NAME plus libsupport:<library> cover the prelude, record blocks and shadow values. Also covered: DSL builtins, facts params and oracle parameters. cost/elapsed cover disch.cost/disch.delay, and perm covers the principal labels. Step/run/obs/runs_ok refs are per action reached (literal actions, or every action for a binder), keyed A_<name>, with src/doc/*_doc removed everywhere. Synthesized helpers map to {template_id, template_version} via refs.TEMPLATES (extensible for I15's at_site/site_hit). law_hash takes lib (default: the facts' libraries under root); regress reads libraries from history. Other unit tests cover an observer's defs, library builtins, src/doc invariance, per-action step refs and template refs. Refs are keyed by facts/library construct, which is one-to-one with I11 diagram elements; diagram-element ids are not used as keys. No 0.3 hash had been frozen.

title: The core library cannot prove the lemmas DISCH and coercion guards need, and no generated proof uses it
reproduction: holon/gen/core.py:25-40: the CATALOG has 9 lemmas. The proof classes absurd, nat1, nat2 and bool1 offer only {==}, a hypothesis, ex falso and the induction hypothesis. They never call another lemma and never match three binders. In the clone, each of the following was appended to CATALOG and core.solve() run; all failed with 'core: no candidate proves <name> case i': core_lt_of_le_lt and core_and_lt_add (both already used by mproofs.deadline, mproofs.py:409-433), core_le_trans, and core_one_le_of_lt (a<b -> 1<=b, the shape of the idx-1 guard). mproofs.py:409-433 and 557 still paste M1's hand-proved CORE (core_lt_of_le_lt, core_le_add_l, core_kappa_site, core_and_lt_add). `grep core_ holon/gen/mproofs.py` finds no generated proof calling the imported core (C.*). Every M2+ proof imports the core and none uses it, so the I8-P4 cost figure (import 0.87x paste) compares unused text. The I8 report's 'they switch to the core library with the first M2 DISCH law' cannot happen with these classes.
plan_or_paper_ref: BUILD_PLAN I8 goal 'Shared lemmas are checked once and imported'; whitepaper 6 core library, 10.3; I15 deliverable mproofs.coercion_guard (idx-1 at :636 PROVED); I31 DISCH
suggested_fix: Add a proof class that composes catalog lemmas (candidates include calls to earlier lemmas, in catalog order). Add a 3-binder nat3 class and Nat.sub lemmas (sub_add, le_of_lt, lt_of_le_lt, le_trans). Move the pasted M1 CORE lemmas into the catalog and make the M2+ deadline, chain_revert and I15 coercion_guard generators call them through C. Test that a generated M2 proof calls a core lemma and fails when that lemma is omitted.
resolution: holon/gen/core.py: two new proof classes, nat3 (match on three binders) and compose (no case split). Every class's candidates now include compositions: calls of EARLIER catalog lemmas, found by first-order matching against a small normaliser of literal-headed Bend terms. Their hypotheses come from the case, from the induction hypothesis, or from a depth-2 call. A successor-congruence candidate covers Nat equations. The catalog grew to 27 lemmas, solved in about 30 s from a fresh build dir and checked under both kernels. It holds M1's hand-pasted CORE lemmas with identical statements, pinned by TestCatalog.test_m1_pasted_core_lemmas_are_catalog_lemmas_with_the_same_statements. It adds transitivity (core_le_trans, core_lt_of_le_lt, core_lt_of_lt_le) and sum monotonicity (core_le_add_mono, core_le_add_left, core_le_succ, core_le_add_self). It also adds the guard-to-subtraction shapes I15's coercion_guard needs: a<b, b>=1, b<=a, !(a<b), !(a>b) give core_le_of_lt, core_one_le_of_lt, core_le_of_ge, core_le_of_not_lt, core_le_of_not_gt; core_sub_add and core_sub_add_of_lt cover a non-truncated Nat.sub. M2+ deadline and chain_revert call the core through C (mproofs.core_ref/efq_ref/core_block). M0/M1 keep the pasted CORE byte for byte (test_m1_disch_proofs_are_unchanged). A generated M2+ proof over the Morph rollup calls core lemmas and fails with 'expected : a filled definition' when any of them is omitted. Other pinning tests in tests_m2/test_core_compose.py: TestCatalog, TestCoreChecks.
resolved_by: audit-fix lane (FX1/FX2), cherry-picked onto the I14+I15 prereg f827be4 (commits b279152..ecbb4b8)

title: Prover separation lets a proof that never imports its law pass: PROVED without the law being checked
reproduction:
Under the separated layout (mpipeline.py:302-313), PROOF.bend lives in gen/proofs/<law>/ with no sibling LAWS.bend, so Bend's rule 'PROOF.bend must import ./LAWS.bend' no longer applies. separated_proof (mpipeline.py:316-321) only rewrites the import line with str.replace; if a generator omits it, nothing notices. Every acceptance point checks only rr.ok plus the LAWS text: implication.py:153, mpipeline.py:433, 475, 539, 569, 635. Probes in the scratch copy: proofs/l2/PROOF.bend = 'import Base
import ../../model/m.bend as M
def helper() -> Nat: 0n' gives 'ALL PROOFS CHECK' under bend and under --verdict (exit 0). The same file colocated with a LAWS.bend gives 'Error: PROOF.bend must import ./LAWS.bend'. End to end: replacing mproofs.GENERATORS with a generator returning 'import Base

def helper() -> Nat:
  0n
' makes statement_diff.check_entry(strengthening_false.json) return ok=True, 'strengthening: L10_sd_small => L10_sd_small checked by bend and BendTT --verdict (class forgetful)'. With the honest generators it is rejected. This contradicts AGENTS rule 6 ('the expected law is present in it') and I10.md's claim that 'the separation does not make a law vacuous'. That probe only covered a file that imports the law.
plan_or_paper_ref: BUILD_PLAN I10 Prover separation; whitepaper §9.4 'Provers have no write access to LAWS/', L14; AGENTS.md rule 6
suggested_fix: At every acceptance point (implication.prove, mpipeline run/param_search/reach_search/negation, G5 and G11 for M2+), require that PROOF.bend imports exactly the relative LAWS path as Laws and defines `def Laws.<law_name>`. Better, check `bend PROOF.bend -o` and require the law symbol to appear as a filled definition. Add a regression test in which the proof omits the import and must not be PROVED.
resolution: Added mpipeline.law_import_problem plus accepted(): a PROOF.bend counts only if it imports exactly its LAWS.bend (the relative path) as Laws. This now applies at holon run's generator loop, the counter-law, param_search, reach_search, decide_negation and implication.prove, and in gate G5 and G11. The probe (bend/notes/p_ir03_import_depth) shows why this is enough: an import-less proof checks vacuously, while an imported but unfilled law is a TODO. The audit's reproduction (every generator replaced by an import-less proof) is now rejected. The gate-side check is in tests_m2/test_gate_ir03.py::TestToyIR03Gate.test_a_proof_that_does_not_import_its_law_fails_g5_and_g11. M0's own pipeline.py (colocated, where Bend's rule applies) was not changed.
resolved_by: audit-fix lane (FX1/FX2), cherry-picked onto the I14+I15 prereg f827be4 (commits b279152..ecbb4b8)

title: G2 never ties a statement-hash change to a STATEMENT_DIFF entry: weaken a law, update the registry, and G2 passes
reproduction: gate.py:586-623: G2 = registry hashes match plus check_file(STATEMENT_DIFF) accepts every line. Nothing compares the registry with its committed predecessor or requires an entry for a changed hash. In the clone, adding premise {eq:[{var:j},{nat:0}]} to laws/M1/L_undo_cancel.json and writing its new law_hash into laws/M1/REGISTRY.json gives Gate('M1').g2_registry() -> {'passed': True, 'detail': 'all statement and facts hashes match the registry'}, and check_file(STATEMENT_DIFF.jsonl) -> [] with the log empty. plan_or_paper_ref: BUILD_PLAN I10 Goal ('every statement change goes through an auditable channel ... enforced mechanically'); whitepaper §9.3 G2, §9.4
suggested_fix: In G2, for every law whose registry hash differs from the registry at the last commit (read-only git cat-file, as check_file already does), or which was deleted, require an accepted STATEMENT_DIFF entry whose old/new carry exactly those statements.
